To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a dual catalysis system, consisting of N-heterocytic carbene and photoredx catalysis, enables the catalytic asymmetric alpha-acylation of N-substituted tert-amines with aldehydes.

the dual catalysis mode of N-heterocycle carbene (NHC) and photoredoxy catalysis enables the asymmetric α-acylative cross-coupling of tertiary aminium salts and aldehydes with the formation of the C(sp(3))–C(acyl) bond and loss of molecular H(2) with high yields, high diastereomeric and enantioselectivities.

the combination of photoredox and chiral N-hetereocyclic carbene (NHC) catalysis enables the catalytic asymmetric alpha-acylation of N-aryl tertiary amines, which is a new method for the formation of C-C bonds via the activation of a C-H bond.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new catalytic methods for the synthesis of biologically active molecules and natural products.
the development of novel methods that enable the direct functionalization of unactivated substrates.
the development and mechanistic understanding of new catalytic processes for the direct functionalization of C-H bonds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of photoredox and chiral N-hetereocyclic carbene catalysts is a powerful and versatile approach to the asymmetric synthesis of α-substituted tertiary amines.
the combination of photoredox and NHC catalysts is a powerful and versatile approach to C-C bond formation via direct activation of the C-H bonds of tertiary aminium salts.
the combination of photoredox and N-heterocytic carbene catalysis has been used in the first example of catalytic enantioselective α-acylations of tertiary aminium salts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a dual-catalysis mode that enables the direct α-acylation and cross-aldol reaction of tertiary aminium salts with carbonyl compounds.
the photoredox catalyst serves to activate the aldehyde, while the chiral N-hetereocyclic carbene catalyst activates the amine substrate.

the reaction of a tertiary amine with an aldehyde and an ester under visible light irradiation in the presence of a chiral NHC and a photoredox catalyst leads to the corresponding α-acylated tertiary amine with excellent enantioselectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of these two catalytic systems enables the direct use of unreactive aldehydes as coupling partners.

the use of photoredox catalysts as hydrogen atom acceptors in the context of dual catalytic asymmetric transformations is a powerful strategy that allows for the use of simple, bench-stable starting materials.
the combination of photoredox and chiral organocatalysis can be utilized in a dual catalysis fashion to enable the direct activation of aldehydes for C-C bond forming transformations.
